title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 467-469). Grothendieck is classifying forms G of Gl(2)_S, and of its projective quotient GPl(1)_S = PG (his notation for PGL(2), the automorphism group of P^1), using 'modular triples' (ρ, σ, ε_0). Here σ satisfies σ²+1=0 (order 4, image σ̃ of order 2), ρ satisfies ρ²−ρ+1=0 (order 6, image ρ̃ of order 3), and ε_0 = −σ^{-1}ρ is unipotent. These lift the standard generators of SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3.

The 'théorème d'épinglage' (58) on the previous page states two bijections:
- Isom(Gl(2), G) ≅ Tripmod(G);
- Isom(GPl(1), PG) ≅ Tripmod(PG).
Injectivity means a homomorphism or automorphism is determined by its values on ρ and σ. Infinitesimally this says the common centralizer of ρ and σ is the centre (59). In the projective case it says (60) N'_ρ ∩ N'_σ = Cent.

This page defines (61) N'_ρ, N'_σ ⊂ Gl(2)_S as the stabilizers of ρ̃ and σ̃, i.e. {g | gρg^{-1} = ερ, ε scalar}, and similarly for σ. He notes that ε² = 1 necessarily (take determinants).

The Remark asks two questions.
- Projective case: is GPl(1)_Z, viewed as an 'absolute' fpqc sheaf of groups on Spec Z, generated by three homomorphisms
  - Z/2 → PGL_2 (α ↦ σ̃_0^α),
  - Z/3 → PGL_2 (β ↦ ρ̃_0^β),
  - G_a → PGL_2 (λ ↦ ε̃_0(λ), the unipotent subgroup),
  subject to the single relation (62) ρ̃_0^{-1} σ̃_0 ε̃_0(1) = 1?
- Linear case: the analogous question for Gl(2)_Z, with Z/4 and Z/6 in place of Z/2 and Z/3, and relation (63) ρ_0^{-1} σ_0 ε_0(1) = ρ_0³ = σ_0².

The aim is a scheme-theoretic, 'arithmetic' presentation of the group scheme. It would extend the classical amalgam presentation of the modular group by adjoining the additive group, so that 'épinglages' of forms correspond exactly to triples satisfying the relations. The next page then tries to show that most of the defining conditions (51)-(56) on triples are redundant.
errors: Linear case: the proposed generators cannot generate Gl(2)_Z. σ_0 and ρ_0 have determinant 1 and ε_0(λ) is unipotent, so everything generated lies in SL_2. The determinant map Gl(2) → G_m is not hit. The analogous question only makes sense for SL(2)_Z, presumably with the centre μ_2 handled separately.

Projective case, the presentation fails as stated. Eliminating ρ̃ via ρ̃ = σ̃ ε̃(1), the amalgam presheaf has, on a connected ring R, the value (Z/2 * Z/3) *_Z G_a(R) = PSL_2(Z) *_Z R, where Z = ⟨T⟩ and T = ε(1).

Why this has a kernel: take a field K ⊇ Q(t) with t transcendental. In SL_2/PGL_2, w(t) = x_+(t) x_-(−1/t) x_+(t), where x_-(s) = σ x_+(−s) σ^{-1}. The relation h(t) x_+(s) h(t)^{-1} = x_+(t²s), with h(t) = w(t) w(1)^{-1}, holds in PGL_2(K). Written in the generators, it is a reduced alternating word in PSL_2(Z) *_Z K (t, 1/t ∉ Z; σ ∉ ⟨T⟩), hence nontrivial.

fpqc sheafification cannot kill this element. A faithfully flat K-algebra maps to some field L, and the word stays reduced over L. So the kernel survives and the proposed presentation is not injective.
Repair: Steinberg/Tits-type relations involving all λ (torus action, w(t)-relations) must be added, as in Demazure's generators-and-relations theorem for split reductive groups (SGA3 Exp. XXIII).
Minor: for ρ (trace 1) the scalar in N'_ρ is in fact forced to be ε = 1, not merely ε² = 1. Only for σ (trace 0) can ε = −1 occur, e.g. conjugation by diag(1,−1).

ideas.what: Classification of forms of GL_2 / PGL_2 over a base S, and their isomorphisms, by 'modular triples' (ρ,σ,ε_0) satisfying the modular-group relations (théorème d'épinglage)
ideas.modern_name: Pinnings (épinglages) of reductive group schemes, expressed via modular-group generators instead of torus + root groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Demazure–Grothendieck (SGA3) for pinnings; the modular-triple form seems specific to these notes
ideas.where_published: Standard épinglages in SGA3 Exp. XXIII; the triple version not known to me in print

ideas.what: Stabilizers of an element up to scalars, and the triviality N'_ρ ∩ N'_σ = centre
ideas.modern_name: Projective centralizers / normalizers; rigidity of the pair (S, ST)

ideas.what: Question: is PGL_2 over Spec Z, as an fpqc group sheaf, the amalgam of constant Z/2, Z/3 and G_a modulo ρ^{-1}σε(1)=1? Similarly SL/GL_2 with Z/4, Z/6
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of Chevalley group schemes by generators and relations (Steinberg/Tits/Demazure); sheaf-theoretic amalgams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinberg (1962) for abstract groups, Tits, Demazure SGA3 XXIII for group schemes

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes presenting the group scheme PGL_2/Spec Z as an fpqc sheaf amalgam of the arithmetic modular-group presentation Z/2 * Z/3 with G_a, glued along ε(1). He asks to settle it, together with the SL/GL_2 analogue with Z/4, Z/6. As stated the answer is negative: the amalgam's sections over a field are PSL_2(Z) *_Z K, which maps non-injectively onto PGL_2(K). One must add relations for all λ (torus/Weyl relations). The interesting residual question is a minimal set of extra relations mixing the constant modular group with G_a. Equivalently: what is the 'modular' version of Demazure's presentation?
missed.quote: Il est plausible, que GPl(1)_Z — en tant que faisceau en groupes "absolu" (sur Spec Z) pour fpqc, est engendré par les hom. Z/2Z → …, Z/3Z → …, G_a → … satisfaisant la seule relation (62) — il vaudrait bien la peine de tirer cette question au clair
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a mild curiosity linking the modular group's amalgam structure with scheme-theoretic presentations of SL_2/PGL_2, in the spirit of the anabelian/Teichmüller programme. It is not a significant open problem, since the naive version fails and the corrected version is essentially Steinberg/Demazure.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished speculative question. As formulated it is false (and the GL(2) version is ill-posed because of the determinant), and the corrected version reduces to known Steinberg/Demazure presentations. Mildly interesting as a link between the modular-group amalgam and group-scheme presentations, but not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'Gl(1)_Z' in the Remark should read 'GPl(1)_Z' (Grothendieck's notation for PGL(2) = Aut P^1); the image shows 'GP(1)_Z' / 'GPl(1)_Z' in all four occurrences.
The marginal note reads 'NB on a nécessairement ε² = 1', correctly placed next to (61).
The struck-out text after 'plausible, que' reads roughly 'les sous-groupes, résultats, de la' (crossed out).
In (63) the left side is ρ_0^{-1}σ_0 ε̃_0(1); in the image the tilde is on ε_0 only.
